questions.q: What is the first step this lesson recommends before trying to fix a slow Tableau workbook?
options: Record its actual behavior with Performance Recording instead of guessing at the cause
Immediately delete all calculated fields
Switch every live connection to an extract without checking anything first
Rebuild the workbook from scratch
questions.explain: The lesson's core principle is 'measure before you optimize' — Performance Recording turns a vague feeling of slowness into specific, named events with real durations.

questions.q: What does the Timeline view in a performance recording show?
options: Every recorded event plotted as a bar across elapsed time, showing when and how long each one took relative to the others
Only the single slowest event in the entire recording
The literal SQL or query text sent to the data source
A list of every calculated field in the workbook
questions.explain: The Timeline lays out events chronologically across elapsed time, which helps distinguish a one-time cost (like an initial extract build) from a recurring one (like a query that reruns on every filter change).

questions.q: What does the Events view do differently from the Timeline view?
options: It sorts the same recorded events by duration, longest first, making the actual bottleneck immediately visible
It only shows events related to geocoding
It shows events in alphabetical order by event name
It replaces the need for the Query view entirely
questions.explain: The Events view reorders the same data by duration — whatever sits at the top of that sorted list is where optimization effort should go first.

questions.q: According to the lesson, which of these is a real, recurring cause of Tableau workbook slowness?
options: Complex LOD expressions or table calculations being recomputed on every render
Having more than one worksheet in a workbook
Using the Marks card at all
Publishing a workbook to Tableau Public instead of Tableau Server
questions.explain: Complex calculations recalculated repeatedly are a genuine, common performance cost — one of several categories (data connection, extract generation, calculations, view density, dashboard load, geocoding) the lesson names.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say 'it feels slow' is not a diagnosis?
options: Because a real diagnosis names a specific event and duration (e.g., a 4.2-second query) that can be acted on and re-verified, rather than a vague impression
Because Tableau workbooks are never actually slow
Because performance can only be judged by an IT administrator
Because feelings about speed are always inaccurate and should be ignored entirely
questions.explain: A performance recording converts a vague impression into a specific, falsifiable finding — naming exactly which event took how long — which is what makes it possible to fix the right thing and confirm the fix worked.
